newsitem.title: MEXICO: GMexico sees operating margin hurt by copper price.
newsitem.headline: GMexico sees operating margin hurt by copper price.

text.p: Mexican mining firm Grupo Minera Mexico said on Friday that volatile copper prices should hurt second half operating margins by at least 10 percent compared with the year's first half.

"If copper prices continue to fall during the second semester, our real margins will fall between 10 and 15 percent compared to those we had in June," Carlos Oyanguren, assistant finance director at the company, told Reuters in an interview.
Copper prices have plunged to between 94 and 96 cents during the first half of this year from about $1.40 per pound last year.
"We got accustomed last year to margins above 50 percent, which are impossible to sustain in any industry," he said.
Grupo Mexico's operating margin was 45.75 percent in 1995 and were about 40.5 percent in June, 1996, the company said.
Analysts expect Grupo Mexico's operating margin to end the year at about 34.50 percent.
On the bright side, Oyanguren said average copper prices during 1996 will be higher than in some recent years.

"We expect average copper prices of $1.10 per pound for 1996. In 1994, that was $1.07," he said. He added that the company was insulated somewhat from price fluctuations because it had 65 percent of its production insured.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom 525 7289565
